title: Increment and decrement operators
context: What is the difference between i++ and ++i? What does `i = i++` do?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `i++` is post-increment. It returns the old value and then adds one. `++i` is pre-increment. It adds one first and returns the new value. In `i = i++`, the old value is read and stored, then the variable is incremented, and the assignment overwrites that increment. So after `int i = 1; i = i++;` the value is still 1. Avoid writing code like this.

points.title: Post versus pre
points.why: The position of ++ decides whether the old or new value is used in the expression.

points.title: i = i++ does not add
points.why: The assignment overwrites the increment, so the variable keeps its original value.
